motion: Ambur biryani is better than anything in Chennai

rounds.text: Chennai has range that Ambur can't match: seeraga samba mutton, Hyderabadi-style dum, Dindigul-style places, all within one city. Saying one town's style beats everything in a city of this size ignores the best kitchens here, many run by families that have cooked for three generations.

Range isn't quality. Ambur has perfected one thing: chilli-paste masala, tender meat, rice that isn't drowned in ghee. You can eat a full plate and not feel heavy. Most Chennai biryani is either too oily or too mild. Ambur gets the balance right, plate after plate.

You're comparing Ambur's best with Chennai's average. Compare best with best: Chennai's old seeraga samba places match Ambur on balance and beat it on aroma. And many 'Ambur biryani' shops are in Chennai already, so the city has your favourite too.

Ambur shops in Chennai prove my point: Chennai imports the style because it's better. And they still don't taste the same as in Ambur, where the meat is fresher and the masala is made fresh each morning. The original wins.
The motion says 'better than anything in Chennai'. One delicious style doesn't beat a whole city's best. Chennai gives you Ambur-style and much more.

A city's variety doesn't make any single plate better. Put the best Ambur plate next to the best Chennai plate, and Ambur wins on taste, balance and how you feel after. That's the only test that matters.
